description: A production control manager must finalize the sequence and startup controls for three heat-treatment batches on Furnace 7 during the next production window, with input from maintenance, quality, logistics, and safety.

shared_context.S1: Furnace 7 is available for the next production window and is scheduled to process batches R, Q, and P.
shared_context.S2: Maya makes the final production sequence and startup-control decision for Furnace 7.
shared_context.S3: The three batches are all approved for Furnace 7, and production control normally sequences them during the daily cross-functional huddle.
shared_context.S4: At the huddle, Maya records the proposed sequence and obtains a sign-off from maintenance, quality, logistics, and process safety before releasing the furnace schedule.

PF1.text: Jon's maintenance inspection found that Furnace 7's thermocouple calibration certificate expires before this production window; the required recalibration takes exactly 2 hours, but he has not updated the maintenance board because the inspection was completed after the morning planning cutoff.

PF2.text: Priya confirmed from the customer control plan that batch Q requires exactly 15 first-piece hardness tests to be completed and held for review before the batch is released; the control plan was revised yesterday and has not yet been attached to the production traveler.

PF3.text: Carlos found that the staged alloy charge for batch R will oxidize if it remains at the furnace bay for more than 4 hours, so R must run first in this window; he learned this from the material supplier's handling note received this morning and has not entered it into the scheduling system.

PF4.text: Elena's pre-window safety check found that Furnace 7's installed gas analyzer failed its bump test; safety procedure requires replacing it with the available spare before any heat-treatment run, and she has not filed the check record because the inspection is still awaiting electronic sign-off.

acceptance_conditions: Batch R must run before batches Q and P.
Furnace 7 must be recalibrated before the production window.
The recalibration must be scheduled for exactly 2 hours.
Exactly 15 first-piece hardness tests must be required for batch Q.
The failed gas analyzer must be replaced before any heat-treatment run.
The schedule must include a commitment to perform the recalibration.
The schedule must include a commitment to replace the gas analyzer.

content_checks.C1: decisions['furnace_sequence'] == 'R, Q, P' or decisions['furnace_sequence'] == 'R → Q → P'

decisive_facts.why: The expired thermocouple certificate changes the startup plan from ordinary production to a required recalibration lasting exactly 2 hours and requiring a recalibration commitment.
The revised customer control plan changes batch Q's first-piece requirement from the unspecified routine check to exactly 15 hardness tests.
The four-hour oxidation limit changes the sequence to R-Q-P, and only this fact explains why batch R must be scheduled first.
The failed bump test changes the startup equipment decision from using the installed analyzer to replacing it with the spare and recording that replacement commitment.
